program_name: Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing (Italian official designation: Corso di laurea magistrale in Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing). The programme name is used in English on both the Italian and English UNIUD course pages; there is no separate translated Italian title. Referred to on the dedicated microsite as "Master's Degree (Laurea Magistrale) in Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing".
level: master (Italian second-cycle degree / laurea magistrale, 120 ECTS, 2 years, conventional in-person delivery)
teaching_language: English. Fully English-taught. The UNIUD course record states 'Lingua di erogazione: Inglese', the microsite states the programme is 'entirely taught in English', and UNIUD's Additional Notice to the Study Prospectus 2026/2027 lists it first in the 'List of Master's degree courses taught entirely in English'.
campus: Udine (Sede: Udine). Teaching is hosted by DPIA - Polytechnic Department of Engineering and Architecture, Via delle Scienze 206, 33100 Udine, Italy. No branch or partner campus outside Udine (the Kyoto Institute of Technology link is a double-degree mobility option, not a delivery campus).
degree_class: Interclass (interclasse) LM-31 Ingegneria gestionale / LM-33 Ingegneria meccanica. The UNIUD course record lists both classes; the Engineering Study Prospectus 2026/27 writes it as 'Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing (interclasse LM-31 Ingegneria Gestionale / LM-33 Ingegneria Meccanica)'. Two curricular tracks are offered - Track M (Metals, production and materials) and Track E (Processing, Energy & Environment) - and students on the Mechanical Engineering track are identified with LM-33; the final class is determined within the programme. [uncertain] No official UNIUD page explicitly states the exact moment the class is chosen (the research brief assumes it is selected at graduation); this specific timing was not confirmed on any official page.
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero). No entrance ranking test, no numerus clausus, no TOLC and no SAT. Admission is by verification of curricular requirements plus an assessment of personal preparation by the programme's Advisor / didactic committee. For applicants with a foreign qualification, admission runs through a compulsory online pre-evaluation (prior assessment) on the Elix-Forms platform, which functions as a rolling, committee-based screening rather than a competitive selection.
access_type_detail: 'Accesso libero' - explicitly stated on the official UNIUD course page (field 'Accesso: accesso libero'). The programme is NOT 'programmazione locale' and therefore has no published total intake cap. This is confirmed by the Engineering Study Prospectus 2026/27, which lists locally capped courses separately (e.g. Tecniche dell'Edilizia e del Territorio, 50 places plus 3 reserved for non-EU students) and lists Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing only as an active master's course with 'Anni di corso attivati: tutti' and no place limit. UNIUD's Additional Notice also excludes it from the list of nationally and locally regulated courses requiring an admission test.
academic_requirements:
A Bachelor's degree (first-cycle / laurea triennale) with a major in engineering.

Italian qualification route: a Bachelor's degree of class L-9 (Industrial Engineering) is required, with at least 45 CFU/ECTS in the basic-training scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD: CHIM/03, CHIM/07, FIS/01, FIS/03, INF/01, ING-INF/05, MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08, MAT/09, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02) and at least 80 CFU in the characterising sectors (FIS/04, ICAR/01, ICAR/03, ICAR/08, ING-IND/01 to ING-IND/35, ING-INF/04, ING-INF/06, ING-INF/07). For a.y. 2026/27 the SSD list in force before D.M. 639/2024 applies. Applicants short of the minimum credits must make them up before enrolment by passing additional single courses (corsi singoli).

Foreign qualification route: a Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field, covering a broad range of industrial disciplines (e.g. Chemical, Mechanical, Process & Environment, Energy, Materials Science, Manufacturing). The foreign first-cycle degree must be official, issued by an accredited institution within its own education system, and must give access to equivalent second-cycle courses in that system. Minimum GPA requirement: the final grade of the bachelor degree must be not less than 3/4 of the maximum possible.

Personal preparation: after curricular requirements are verified, the didactic committee assesses previous academic record and, where needed, holds a test or interview. Candidates whose final degree mark was not lower than 90/110 are exempt from that test/interview (Italian-system rule).

English: B2 CEFR is a formal admission requirement, verified by the programme's Advisory Committee.
entry_exam_or_test: No competitive entrance examination (no TOLC, no CEnT-S, no SAT, no written admission test). What exists is (a) an assessment of personal preparation by the didactic committee, possibly through a test or interview, and (b) for international applicants an online pre-evaluation by the Academic/Advisor Committee, which may include an online interview - notably to test English proficiency when no language certificate is provided. The Advisor Committee meets on a monthly basis whenever student applications are present (rolling admission).
entry_test_name_and_deadline:
Name: not a named standardised test. It is an 'eventuale prova o colloquio' (possible test or interview) run by the programme's didactic/Advisor Committee, plus - for foreign-degree applicants - an online pre-evaluation with a possible online interview on the Elix-Forms procedure.

Deadlines: the interview/pre-evaluation is tied to the Elix-Forms application windows - 01/02/2026 to 10/09/2026 for applicants residing in the EU, and 01/02/2026 to 31/05/2026 for applicants residing in non-EU countries. The Advisor Committee meets monthly, so there is no single fixed test date; a calendar of tests/interviews is published by the university when applicable.

Exemption: 'Sono esonerati da tale prova o colloquio i candidati che abbiano riportato nell'esame di laurea una votazione non inferiore a 90/110' - candidates with a final degree mark of at least 90/110 are exempt from the test/interview.

OFA / additional learning requirements: UNIUD does not apply OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi) at master's level. Instead, credit shortfalls must be cleared BEFORE enrolment by passing extra single courses ('corsi singoli') - so missing credits cannot be carried into the degree the way an OFA can. Consequently the credit top-up must be completed before matriculation, not after.
reserved_places_non_eu: A quota of places reserved for students residing in non-EU countries exists for every UNIUD degree course. The Additional Notice to the Study Prospectus 2026/2027 states: 'For each degree course, an annual quota of places is reserved for students residing in non-EU countries. The quota for the academic year 2026/2027 can be found in Annex 1 of this Notice.' [uncertain] The exact number for this programme could not be established: Annex 1 for a.y. 2026/2027 is referenced in the Notice but is not bundled inside the published 9-page PDF and no separate Annex 1 file for 2026/2027 was found on uniud.it (only an older 24/25 annex URL is indexed, and it no longer resolves to a document). Because the course is 'accesso libero', the non-EU quota is an administrative visa-related contingent rather than a competitive cap.
admin_seat_university: University of Udine (Università degli Studi di Udine, UNIUD) is the sole administering university. Academic home: DPIA - Dipartimento Politecnico di Ingegneria e Architettura. This is not an inter-university (interateneo) programme: application, pre-evaluation, admission, enrolment (immatricolazione), tuition fees and the degree are all handled by UNIUD. A double-degree option exists with the Kyoto Institute of Technology (Japan) for students on the Mechanical Engineering / LM-33 track, but that is an optional mobility agreement and does not shift the administrative seat.
course_status_flag: Active and fully open to new enrolments - NOT 'ad esaurimento'. The Engineering Study Prospectus 2026/27 lists the programme among the active master's courses with 'Anni di corso attivati: tutti' (all course years activated), and it appears in the 2026/2027 Additional Notice list of English-taught master's degrees. No phase-out, suspension or teach-out notice appears on any official UNIUD page.
language_requirements:
English: certified knowledge at B2 level or equivalent on the CEFR scale is required. The certificate must clearly state the achieved level.

Accepted certificate providers (UNIUD official list): Cambridge English Language Assessment; Trinity College London; IELTS; TOEFL; Pearson Edexcel - Test of English Academic (PTE Academic); Pearson General English; Oxford Test of English; LanguageCert International ESOL; Gatehouse Awards Classic; British Council - Aptis ESOL General; British Council - Aptis ESOL Advanced.

Exemptions: applicants who completed a school programme taught in English (IB diplomas, multilingual schools, etc.) and native English speakers (per the UK gov.uk English-speaking-country list) are exempt from submitting a B2 certificate.

No-certificate route: a pre-evaluation application may be submitted without the certificate if the applicant is awaiting the exam or the issuance of the certificate; and where a B2-or-equivalent certificate is absent, the competent Academic Committee may assess English skills through an online interview. The programme microsite confirms: 'the Advisor Committee will arrange an interview if needed, e.g., to test your language proficiency if no certification is provided.' However, obtaining the certificate remains a necessary requirement for completing enrolment.

Italian: no Italian language requirement for this programme, since it is taught entirely in English. (Italian B2 via CLIQ certification - CELI, CILS, CERTIT, PLIDA - applies only to Italian-taught courses.)
english_level_exception: No exception applies to this programme - the standard B2 CEFR requirement holds. The only UNIUD English-level exception is for a different course: 'For the Master's degree course in Management Engineering, the required level of English language proficiency is B1.' Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing is explicitly a B2 course, stated both in the Additional Notice and in the Engineering Study Prospectus footnote: applicants 'need to demonstrate an ability in English at B2 level, verified by the Advisory Committee of the program.' For partially English-taught courses UNIUD requires B2 in both Italian and English - not applicable here.
english_cert_validity_years: 5 years. UNIUD general rule, applied to this programme: 'Only certificates obtained within the last 5 years will be considered valid. Certificates must clearly indicate the achieved level.' No programme-specific deviation from the 5-year rule was found. (Note: a separate 5-year rule exists at UNIUD for the Management Engineering master's, where the bachelor degree itself must have been obtained in the last five years - that rule does NOT apply to Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing.)
teaching_language_partial_flag: Fully English ('tamamen İngilizce'). 100% of the programme is delivered in English; there is no Italian-language curriculum branch and no partially-English arrangement. Evidence: UNIUD course record 'Lingua di erogazione: Inglese'; the programme is on UNIUD's official list of 'Degrees taught entirely in English' and in the Additional Notice 'List of Master's degree courses taught entirely in English'; the microsite states it is 'entirely taught in English'. The two internal tracks (Track M - Metals, production and materials; Track E - Processing, Energy & Environment) are both English-taught curricular options, not a language split.
application_deadline_eu: 10/09/2026 (10 September 2026), with the window opening 01/02/2026. Applies to prospective students residing in an EU country and/or holding a foreign qualification, applying through the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation platform: 'Applications for admission to master's degree courses taught in Italian and in English must be submitted on the Elix-Forms platform between 01/02/2026 and 10/09/2026.' Because the Advisor Committee meets monthly and enrolment closes 5 October 2026, applying late in this window leaves very little margin for the 30-working-day decision plus enrolment; early application is strongly advisable. Applicants holding an Italian bachelor's degree do not use Elix-Forms - they follow the ordinary domestic immatricolazione procedure within the 9 July - 5 October 2026 enrolment window.
application_deadline_non_eu: 31/05/2026 (31 May 2026), with the window opening 01/02/2026. Applies to prospective students residing in a non-EU country who need a study visa: 'Applications for admission to Master's degree courses taught in Italian or English must be submitted through the Elix-Forms platform between 01/02/2026 and 31/05/2026.' This closes more than three months before the EU deadline, to leave time for the eligibility letter, Universitaly pre-enrolment and the consular visa procedure.
universitaly_deadline: 30 June 2026 - a separate, hard deadline distinct from the university's own 31 May 2026 Elix-Forms deadline. Non-EU-resident applicants must create a digital profile on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/first-steps) and submit the digital pre-enrolment application for a UNIUD degree course for a.y. 2026/2027 'by the 30th of June 2026 at the latest. Pre-enrolment applications submitted after the 30th of June 2026 will not be considered.' Documents to attach on Universitaly for a second-cycle course: valid passport; passport-sized photograph; first-cycle university degree (or final/provisional single-cycle master's); and an English language certificate at B2 or equivalent (since the course is English-taught). The sequence is: Elix-Forms pre-evaluation (by 31 May) -> letter of eligibility for enrolment by email -> Universitaly pre-enrolment (by 30 June) -> UNIUD digitally validates and forwards to the consulate -> visa decision by the consulate alone. Pre-enrolment and preliminary acceptance confer no right to a visa or even to a consular appointment. Applicants may enrol only in the course selected on Universitaly, and may not change course or transfer to another Italian university during the first year.
decision_timeline_days: 30 working days from the date of submission of a complete Elix-Forms pre-evaluation application. 'the application will be forwarded for the evaluation to the Academic Committee, which will communicate the outcome of the assessment to the applicant via email within 30 working days from the date of submission.' Only complete applications (with the €20 fee duly paid) are evaluated. The programme's Advisor Committee meets on a monthly basis when applications are present, which is what makes the process effectively rolling. UNIUD's Application Presentation Guide adds a practical note: applicants should use the 'Re-send the email' button only if no answer has arrived within 4 weeks. Possible outcomes communicated by email: DENIED (with reason), APPROVED, or APPROVED WITH RESTRICTIONS (with reason).
enrolment_window: Matriculation (immatricolazione) for master's degrees at UNIUD for a.y. 2026/2027: opens 9 July 2026 and closes 5 October 2026 at 12:00 noon. A late-enrolment extension may be granted by the Rector for serious and justified reasons until 31 March 2027, on submission of a late-enrolment request bearing a €16.00 revenue stamp. Students who obtained their bachelor's degree after 5 October 2026 do not need to file a late-enrolment request. Because the course is accesso libero, there is no first-come-first-served place exhaustion and no chronological-order ranking for this programme (that mechanism exists at UNIUD only for locally capped courses). Non-EU visa applicants must nonetheless clear the Elix-Forms (31 May) and Universitaly (30 June) deadlines well before this window, and the English certificate must be in hand to complete enrolment even if the pre-evaluation was approved without it.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.uniud.it/en/student-services/tuition-fees/tuition-fees?set_language=en - the official UNIUD tuition and fee-waiver page linked directly from the programme microsite. The microsite summarises: 'University tuition fees per academic year consist of fees and contributions, regional dues and stamp duty. University tuition fees might vary from a minimum of € 16.00 (for fee-waiver eligible students) up to € 2,026.00 (full fee).' Separate from tuition, the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation application carries a non-refundable €20.00 fee, and a late-enrolment request requires a €16.00 revenue stamp.

uncertainty_notes:
1) NON-EU RESERVED PLACES - unresolved. The 2026/2027 Additional Notice confirms a per-course non-EU quota exists and points to 'Annex 1 of this Notice', but Annex 1 is not included in the published 9-page PDF (either language version) and no standalone 2026/2027 Annex 1 file was located anywhere on uniud.it. Only an older 24/25 annex URL is indexed by search engines and it no longer resolves to a document. The exact reserved number for this programme is therefore unknown and should be requested from studenti@uniud.it.

2) DEGREE-CLASS CHOICE TIMING - partly unresolved. LM-31 / LM-33 interclass status is confirmed on official pages, and the course description ties Track M / the Mechanical Engineering track to LM-33 for double-degree eligibility. But no official UNIUD page states explicitly when the student's class is formally fixed (at enrolment, at study-plan submission, or at graduation). The research brief's assumption that it is chosen at graduation is plausible for Italian interclass degrees but was not verifiable from official sources.

3) NO INTERATENEO/JOINT EXCEPTION APPLIES. Unlike some other programmes in this dataset, this one is administered entirely by UNIUD. There is no partner university seat handling admission or fees. The Kyoto Institute of Technology relationship is an optional double-degree mobility agreement for LM-33-track students only; students still enrol at, pay fees to, and are admitted by UNIUD. Do not treat it as a joint-degree admission route.

4) TWO DIFFERENT DEADLINE FAMILIES MUST NOT BE MERGED. (a) Elix-Forms pre-evaluation: 01/02/2026-10/09/2026 for EU residents, 01/02/2026-31/05/2026 for non-EU residents. (b) Universitaly pre-enrolment for the study visa: 30 June 2026, non-EU only, later than the Elix-Forms non-EU deadline but earlier than the EU one. (c) Immatricolazione (actual enrolment): 9 July - 5 October 2026 12:00, extendable to 31 March 2027. These are three separate gates.

5) MICROSITE VS. CENTRAL PAGES. The dedicated microsite is the richest source on the academic profile but is silent on deadlines, fees, required documents, the €20 application fee, the 3/4 GPA rule and the 5-year certificate validity. All of those live only in the central UNIUD Additional Notice. The microsite is also silent on whether the course is accesso libero - that is confirmed only on the Italian UNIUD course record. Treat the central pages as authoritative for procedure and the microsite as authoritative for academic content.

6) MINIMUM GPA WORDING. The requirement is expressed as a proportion ('not less than 3/4 of the maximum possible'), not as a fixed grade, so it must be computed against each country's own grading maximum. For an Italian 110-scale degree this is 82.5/110, which is below the separate 90/110 exemption threshold for the personal-preparation interview - two different thresholds that are easy to confuse.

7) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE TIMING NUANCE. A pre-evaluation may be submitted without the certificate (if awaiting the exam or its issuance), and the Committee may substitute an online interview when no certificate exists. But the Notice also states obtaining the certificate 'remains a necessary requirement for completing enrolment', and the Universitaly document list requires a B2 English certificate for English-taught courses. For non-EU visa applicants these two statements are in practical tension: the interview route may satisfy academic pre-evaluation while the Universitaly/consular stage may still expect a certificate. Applicants without a certificate should confirm with studenti@uniud.it before relying on the interview route.

8) OFA. UNIUD applies no OFA (additional learning obligations) at master's level for this course; credit shortfalls must be cleared before enrolment via 'corsi singoli'. If a field elsewhere in this dataset expects an OFA threshold, the correct value here is 'not applicable'.

9) ACADEMIC YEAR SCOPE. All dates above are for a.y. 2026/2027, current as verified on 2026-09-06. The EU Elix-Forms window (to 10/09/2026) is closing within days of this verification date; the non-EU window (31/05/2026) and the Universitaly deadline (30/06/2026) have already passed for 2026/2027. Figures must be re-verified for 2027/2028, when a new Additional Notice is published (UNIUD publishes the Prospectus annually, historically in June).

10) EXCLUDED FIELD BUNDLE (recorded here per fields.yaml note, not as separate fields): application platform = Elix-Forms (per-programme link https://goto.uniud.it/to/623), with payment via PagoPA; application fee = €20.00 non-refundable; tuition = €16.00 (fee-waiver eligible) to €2,026.00 (full fee) per year, ISEE-based waivers described on the tuition page; minimum GPA = final bachelor grade not less than 3/4 of the maximum possible; selection interview = not automatic, arranged by the Advisor Committee if needed (notably when no English certificate is provided); dedicated programme website = https://industrial-engineering-sustainable-manufacturing.uniud.it ; double-degree partner = Kyoto Institute of Technology (Japan), 'International MASC in Mechanical Engineering', LM-33 / Mechanical Engineering track only, selective.
